action_summary: Two rename rows declare the same verb and tie on the sentence's lexical evidence, so only the file can say which object is being renamed. Measured on main 573e735b, in the repository: "Rename old_name to new_name in <file>." -- where old_name is a def in that file -- was answered FAIL__RAW_GOAL_COMPILATION_GAP with the selected row python.refactor.rename_parameter.v1 and old_param:not_stated, while the identical edit with the words "the function" PASSED. The noun was doing work no noun should do. The mirror shape was worse: "Rename text to value in <file>.", where text is a PARAMETER of norm, PASSED with python.refactor.rename_symbol.v1 and left "def value(text, scale=1)" -- the function's public name changed and the parameter kept its own. declared_input_derivation_v1 now proves both readings against the stated file's AST (QUALNAME_PROVED_FROM_STATED_SOURCE_AST for a def, PARAM_PROVED_FROM_STATED_SOURCE_AST for a parameter) and proves neither when the file does not contain the name. Measured after: all four rename shapes PASS with the right object and "Rename nothing_here to something in <file>." still refuses.
